system_prompt: You write Terraform and Dockerfiles that exactly match an existing project's conventions. Output ONLY the requested file contents in the exact structure asked for — no markdown fences, no explanation before, between, or after the files.
task:
The reference files show this project's existing pattern: a root Terraform module (terraform/main.tf, terraform/variables.tf) that declares the AWS provider exactly once and calls a child module, and a child module (terraform/modules/storage) that declares its own typed variables and has no provider block of its own. Follow that exact pattern to add two new child modules and wire both into root.

New module 1: terraform/modules/table — a DynamoDB table. Requirements: billing_mode PAY_PER_REQUEST, hash_key "id" of type String, point_in_time_recovery enabled, server_side_encryption enabled, and a variable table_name (type string, no default) that the table's name comes from. Export an output named table_name.

New module 2: terraform/modules/queue — an SQS queue pair for failed-write alerting. A primary queue (variable queue_name, type string, no default) with a redrive_policy pointing at a dead-letter queue named "${var.queue_name}-dlq" with maxReceiveCount 5, and the dead-letter queue itself. Export outputs queue_url and dlq_url.

Wire both into root: add module "audit_table" and module "alert_queue" blocks in terraform/main.tf, each calling its module with the relevant variable passed explicitly, plus matching outputs for each. Add matching new variables (table_name, queue_name — both type string, with defaults) to terraform/variables.tf. Do not add a second provider block anywhere — only the root module declares one, matching the existing modules/storage convention exactly.

Also: this project (package.json, src/index.js, both shown for reference) has no Dockerfile yet. Add one. It's a plain JS app with no separate compile/build step — install dependencies from package.json and start src/index.js.
